title: Simplify Path
summary: Return the lexical canonical form of an absolute Unix-style path.
statement: Return the lexical canonical form of an absolute Unix-style path. Skip empty and '.' components, resolve '..' without moving above root, and retain all other names literally. Use one leading slash and one separator between names; only root '/' ends with a slash. This is a string-processing exercise and does not inspect the actual filesystem.
constraints: 1–3000 characters, starting with '/'; characters are English letters, digits, '.', '/', or '_'.
Ignore empty components and '.'. '..' removes a preceding component if one exists; it cannot go above root.
Other components, including '...' and '.cache', are literal names. Return one leading slash, single separators, and no trailing slash except for root '/'. No filesystem access is needed.
hints: Resolve whole components between slashes, not individual dot characters.
Keep the currently resolved directory names on a stack.
Skip empty and '.' components, pop for '..' when possible, otherwise append the literal name; join with one leading slash.
Root remains '/'. Names like '...' and '.cache' must survive unless a later '..' removes them.
editorial: Split at slashes and maintain a stack of resolved directory names. A parent component cancels the newest surviving name, while a current-directory or empty component changes nothing. Join the stack under one leading slash. This is lexical normalization only, independent of actual files or symlinks. The oracle uses posixpath.normpath after normalizing its special double-leading-slash behavior to the problem's single-root rule.

tests.explanation: Remove the trailing separator to obtain /home.
